hse: A near miss was reported on Tuesday when a section of scaffold tube slipped from a bundle being lifted over the pipe rack in [AREA]. The banksman stopped the lift and nobody was beneath the load. [SUB] has been asked to review slinging arrangements for scaffold materials and to brief all crews before the next lift. The incident has been added to the register and [PM] will sample the lifting records next week.

The weekly housekeeping inspection of [AREA] found cable drums stored on the access route to the compressor skid, partly blocking the emergency egress. Two spill kits were found without lids and one fire extinguisher had an expired inspection tag. The site team cleared the route the same afternoon, and [SUB_CONTACT] confirmed that his operatives will check their laydown areas at the start of each shift for the rest of the month.

This month's slips, trips and falls campaign focuses on cable trays, hoses and uneven ground near the tank farm bund walls. Everyone is asked to record trip hazards on the daily walk round card rather than waiting for the weekly inspection. Boot cleaning stations have been placed at two gates to reduce mud carried onto the gravel roads, and [COW] will track the number of reports raised over the next four weeks.

An audit of permits to work over the past fortnight found three hot work permits where the fire watch had not signed the closing section. In each case the work was finished and the area left safe, but the paperwork was incomplete. Permit issuers have been reminded that the fire watch must remain for at least thirty minutes after welding or cutting stops. [PM] has asked for the permit board to be reviewed at the next safety forum.

A small hydraulic oil leak from a telehandler was contained within the drip tray at the jetty laydown yard. The machine was taken out of service, the contaminated absorbent was bagged and placed in the correct waste stream, and the ground has been cleaned. Plant owners have been reminded that all mobile plant must be checked for leaks before leaving the compound each morning and that drip trays must stay in place.

Lock-out tag-out on the gas compression package was reviewed following a query about isolation certificates. Two certificates for the suction scrubber did not show the valve numbers as they appear on the P&ID. Operations have confirmed the correct isolation points and the certificates are being reissued. [CUSTOMER] representatives will be invited to observe the next isolation so that the process can be witnessed.

The LOLER thorough examination of the 25 tonne mobile crane is due next Thursday, and the current certificate was checked at the meeting. The hook block and wire rope inspection records are complete, but the outrigger pad condition report is still outstanding from the hire company. Until it is received, the crane will only be used within the limits of the existing load chart, and lifts will be planned accordingly.

Summer temperatures forecast for next week mean the heat stress plan will be activated. Cool water stations will be checked twice daily at the substation compound, and shaded rest areas will be set up near the pipe bending area. Supervisors should watch for signs of heat exhaustion and encourage regular breaks, particularly for those wearing full chemical suits for painting.

Harness inspection records for [SUB] show that eleven fall arrest harnesses were removed from service during the month because of frayed stitching or damaged buckles. Replacements have been issued and the old harnesses have been cut up and disposed of. Each worker must present their harness for a pre-use check before going onto the pipe rack, and supervisors will log the checks on the daily permit.

A trench for the new drainage run beside the pumphouse was found with a spoil heap less than a metre from the edge. The trench is more than 1.2 metres deep and there was no ladder within the required distance of the workers. Excavation was stopped until the spoil was moved back and a ladder was installed. [SITE_MGR] will ensure that trench inspection records are signed before work resumes each day.

Gas testing of the sump chamber at the water treatment plant recorded oxygen at 20.8 per cent and no hydrocarbon readings above zero. Entry is permitted under the standby arrangement with a trained attendant at the top of the access. Rescue equipment has been checked and placed at the entry point. The attendant must not leave the post, and the entry log must be signed at each change of worker.

Waste segregation has improved across the site since the new skips were labelled to match the local waste contractor's codes. However, mixed general waste was found in the hazardous skip at the north gate. The skip has been emptied and checked, and the labels have been re-fixed. Team leaders are asked to brief their crews on what can and cannot go into each container.

A contractor's operative received a laceration to the palm while handling a sharp-edged flange gasket in the pipework area. First aid was given on site and the worker returned to light duties the same day. The operative was not wearing cut-resistant gloves, and the glove issue for that gang has been reviewed. [SUB_CONTACT] has agreed to introduce a glove check at the start of each shift.

Dust monitoring during grinding and abrasive blasting near the site office recorded readings within the agreed limits, but two readings near the boundary fence were close to the upper threshold. Wetting of the work area and local extraction will continue. The team will reposition the blasting shroud and check the wind direction before starting work each morning to limit dust reaching neighbouring properties.

Portable appliance testing on the temporary power distribution boards is now 90 per cent complete. Three extension leads failed their insulation resistance test and were removed from site. Any lead that is damaged or has missing earthing must be taken out of use immediately and reported to the electrical supervisor. Test labels must be checked before tools are issued.

The fire drill on Wednesday evacuated the whole construction compound in just under six minutes, which is within target. However, two welfare cabins had their fire doors propped open with bricks, and the assembly point roll call took longer than expected because the sign-in sheets were incomplete. Access control and sign-in will be reinforced before the next drill.

Segregated walkways and vehicle routes have been reviewed around the new tanker bay. Delivery drivers were seen reversing without a banksman on two occasions last week. A second banksman will be rostered during peak delivery hours, and yellow lines have been repainted at the turning circle. [CUST_PM] has been notified of the change to the logistics route through the customer gate.

Noise surveys at the compressor enclosure showed that hearing protection signage needs refreshing in two places. Hearing protection is mandatory in the zone, but some visitors have entered without ear defenders. The gatehouse will check visitors for ear protection, and the signs will be replaced with clearer wording and pictograms. Monitoring will continue for the rest of the month.

The scaffold on the south side of the separator vessel was inspected and tagged green following the recent modifications. The inspector noted that a toe board was missing on one lift and a ladder access was positioned incorrectly. Both points were corrected before the tag was signed. Users should check the tag before access and report any damage or loose fittings immediately to the scaffold foreman.

The hand and finger safety campaign this fortnight highlights pinch points on hand tools, pipe clamps and the chain blocks used on the skid frames. Short toolbox talks will be given at the start of each shift, and workers are encouraged to help identify pinch hazards in their work areas. Several gang leaders have volunteered to lead the talks, and [SUB] will provide feedback at the next meeting.

A stock check of personal protective equipment in the stores found adequate supplies of hard hats and safety boots but a shortage of flame-retardant overalls for the welding team. An urgent replacement has been arranged for the required sizes. Until delivery, welders must work only in their existing undamaged overalls, and supervisors will check that clothing is free from oil contamination before welding begins.

Surface water discharge from the attenuation pond was sampled on Monday and sent for laboratory analysis. Results are awaited, and the pond outlet valve remains closed until they are received. Silt fences along the access road have been inspected and two sections need repair after heavy rain. [SITE_MGR] has asked the drainage team to clear the gully gratings before the next forecast rain.

A reversing dumper almost struck a stored gas bottle rack at the laydown yard when its reversing alarm was found to be disconnected. The operator stopped when a banksman signalled, and no contact was made. The machine has been removed from service pending repair. All plant operators have been reminded that alarms and lights must work and that pre-start checks must be recorded in the logbook.

COSHH assessments for the new epoxy coatings have been reviewed, and the data sheets are now available at the paint store. Two containers were found without hazard labels in the coatings store. Labels have been replaced and the chemical register updated. Painters must wear the specified respirators and gloves at all times and must not decant chemicals into unlabelled bottles.

The lifting plan for the 14 tonne column placement was approved this week after review by the lift supervisor. Ground bearing checks were completed and the crane mats were laid out as specified. Exclusion zones will be set up with barriers and signage on the day, and only the appointed signaller will give instructions to the crane operator during the lift.

Permit documents for the switchroom isolation have been checked against the single line diagram. The earthing points listed on the permit did not match the points marked on site, so the permit has been returned to the authorised person for correction. No work on live equipment took place. [COW] will attend the next isolation and sign the earthing record before any worker enters the cordoned area.

Safety observation cards submitted this month totalled 84, of which 61 were positive recognitions and 23 flagged unsafe acts. The most common unsafe acts involved people standing under suspended loads and working without eye protection during grinding. Feedback has been given to the individuals concerned, and the common themes will be covered at next week's toolbox talks.

A spill response drill in the tank farm simulated a diesel release from a damaged transfer hose. The team deployed booms within eleven minutes, and the drain valves were closed as planned. Some confusion arose over who should contact the environment officer, so the call-out list at the bund gate will be updated. A debrief with all shift leaders is scheduled for Friday morning.

Reports of long shifts and fatigue have been reviewed following the increase in weekend working. The rota for the next four weeks has been checked, and no individual is scheduled for more than sixty hours in any seven-day period. Supervisors must watch for signs of tiredness during night shifts and allow rest breaks. Drivers of site vehicles must not drive if they feel unwell or drowsy.

Actions from the last HSE walk round have been closed except for three items: barrier replacement at the pipe rack, updated signage at the gas detection zone, and fire blanket checks in the welding bay. Owners have confirmed dates for all three, and [PM] will report completion at the next progress meeting. Thanks are extended to all crews who reported hazards during the month.
design: A request for information was raised by [SUB] this morning concerning the support spacing on the 150 mm carbon steel line running along the pipe rack in [AREA]. The isometric shows supports at 3.0 m centres, whereas the stress report assumes 2.5 m. [SUB_CONTACT] has asked the design team to confirm which basis governs and to issue a marked-up isometric before the next spool release meeting.

Revision C of the foundation drawing for the compressor skid was issued to site yesterday. The main change is the anchor bolt pattern, which moved to suit the revised baseplate supplied by the vendor. Site engineers have checked the new layout against the setting-out survey and flagged two bolts that clash with an existing embedded plate. [COW] will attend the next walkdown to confirm the resolution.

The 3D model review for [AREA] took place in the design office with representatives from [PM] and the process lead attending. Clashes between the instrument tray and the overhead pipework were discussed in detail. Most were resolved by agreeing small offsets, but three remain open and will be reviewed again once the structural steel layout is updated.

A technical query was submitted regarding the pressure relief valve set pressure shown on the P&ID for the water treatment dosing vessel. The datasheet lists a different value to the one in the cause and effect matrix. The process engineer has been asked to reconcile both documents and confirm the correct figure, so that the valve sizing calculation can be closed out.

Markups received from [CUST_PM] on the electrical single line diagram for the new 11 kV substation include comments on busbar earthing and the protection relay schedule. Several points request additional detail on fault level assumptions. The design team is preparing responses and will return a revised drawing for approval within the agreed review period.

Piping stress analysis for the hot oil line feeding the tank farm has been completed. Nozzle loads on the pump discharge are slightly above the vendor limits in the thermal case. Options include adding a spring hanger or relocating the adjacent anchor. The stress engineer will present both options at the design meeting on Thursday.

Vendor drawing approval for the jetty mooring hooks has been returned with comments. The vendor has been asked to clarify the design load case used for the breasting dolphin and to confirm the weld procedure reference. Brackmoor design staff will check the revised submission against the site specification before releasing the item for fabrication.

Instrument datasheets for the flow transmitters on the gas compression package contain inconsistent process conditions. Two sheets show a line pressure of 42 barg, while the heat and mass balance uses 38 barg. The instrumentation engineer has raised an RFI to confirm the operating case and will update the affected datasheets once the process team responds.

Cable tray routing through the level two cable deck was reviewed during a coordination session. Congestion near the motor control centre was identified as the main issue. Alternative routes were sketched, and the electrical lead agreed to test one option in the model. Revised tray drawings will be issued once the clash report has been rerun.

The HAZOP action log has been reviewed against the current P&IDs. Three actions require a drawing change, including the addition of a low-level trip on the surge drum and a check valve on the nitrogen purge. Design leads have been asked to incorporate these items into the next issue and to record closure in the action tracker.

Drainage falls within the bund for the diesel storage tanks were checked against the civil drawings. The gradient along the northern side appears shallower than specified, which could affect rainwater runoff toward the sump. The civil designer has been asked to confirm levels by survey and advise whether any local regrading is needed.

Isometrics for the 2-inch instrument air headers have been updated to reflect the latest valve tag numbering. Several sheets still show the superseded references from the earlier P&ID issue. The document controller has been asked to recall the old revisions from the site drawing store and issue the corrected set before fabrication begins.

A query has been raised on the cathodic protection design for the buried product pipeline. The anode spacing in the calculation differs from the layout shown on the alignment sheets. The corrosion engineer is checking whether the difference reflects a later soil resistivity survey, and will confirm which version should be used for installation.

The control philosophy for the water treatment plant has been updated to reflect operator comments from the recent review. Changes include revised alarm priorities for the chemical dosing pumps and a new interlock on the filter backwash sequence. The updated document will go to [CUST_PM] for comment before it is adopted as the basis for the software build.

Structural steel connection details for the pipe rack in [AREA] were queried by the erection team. Several gusset plates appear to conflict with the revised beam sizes shown in the latest general arrangement. The structural engineer has agreed to reissue the connection schedule, and erectors will hold work on those bays until the new details are confirmed.

Model review of the compressor building was carried out with [ER] and [COW] present. Walkways and access routes were tested against the maintenance envelope requirements for the reciprocating machine. Two platforms were found to restrict lifting access, and the design team will propose revised steelwork to restore clear routes.

Equipment layout drawings for the new skid-mounted filtration units were marked up by the commissioning team. Their comments focus on isolation valve positions and drain points that are hard to reach. The layout designer will review the markups and reissue the drawing with revised access arrangements shown clearly for operators.

A technical query from [SUB] concerns the material specification for the gaskets on the sulphuric acid line. The drawing calls for a PTFE-based gasket, but the purchase specification lists a graphite option. Engineering has been asked to confirm the chemical compatibility and to issue a single approved specification to both teams.

Pressure testing boundaries on the hydrogen service piping were reviewed against the latest P&IDs. Several spool pieces appear to be missing from the test packs, and two blind flanges are shown in the wrong position. The test engineer has asked for corrected test boundary drawings before the next pneumatic test package is prepared.

The electrical earthing layout for the new substation was checked against the design basis. The earth grid spacing matches the calculation, but the connection points to the transformer neutral are not clearly labelled. A revised drawing has been requested, and the earthing designer will confirm that all bonding conductors are shown with correct sizes.

Gas detector placement on the compressor deck was reviewed against the detection philosophy. Several detectors sit close to a vent stack, which could affect reliability in cross-wind conditions. The process safety engineer will confirm whether relocation is needed, and the layout will be updated once the detector coverage calculation has been rerun.

A revision of the jetty general arrangement has been issued to show the revised fender spacing and the new access ladder. The marine engineer has asked for confirmation of the berthing energy assumptions before the drawing is approved. Design staff are collating the supporting calculations and will send them to [CUST_PM] for review.

Pipe support schedule for the tank farm was checked against the isometric drawings. Some supports listed as guides are shown as anchors on the layout, which would change the stress model. The stress and support designers agreed to align the schedule and reissue it with a clear change list for the site team.

A design check of the sump pump sizing for the process area showed that the calculated flow rate is slightly higher than the figure on the datasheet. The mechanical engineer has asked the vendor to confirm whether the selected pump still meets the head requirement at the higher flow. A response is expected before the datasheet is updated.

Protection relay settings for the 33 kV feeder were checked against the coordination study. The time grading between the incoming breaker and the outgoing feeders appears tight at one location. The protection engineer will rerun the study with the latest transformer data and issue a revised settings schedule for approval.

A model clash review covering the chemical dosing area highlighted interference between a cable tray and a new sample line. The team agreed that the sample line should move, as access to the tray is needed more often. The piping designer will amend the routing and the isometric will be reissued after the next model update.

The commissioning team raised a query about the vent line sizing on the methanol storage tank. The current line appears undersized for the maximum breathing load in the event of rapid filling. The process engineer is checking the calculation and will confirm whether the line size or the filling rate should change.

Revised general arrangement drawings for the water treatment plant were reviewed with the operations team. They asked for clearer labelling of isolation valves, larger access clearances around the lime silo, and a revised location for the eyewash station. The drawing office will incorporate these comments into the next issue for approval.

Vendor documents for the gas turbine lube oil system were received and logged. Several drawings are missing the final stamp, and the bill of materials does not match the control valve list. The document controller has written to the vendor requesting complete sets, and the design lead will review the outstanding items on receipt.

Design freeze for the pipeline pigging facility has been confirmed for the trap layout. Remaining open items relate to the access platform loads and the position of the drain connection. The structural and piping leads are finalising their responses, and the combined design package will be submitted to [ER] once all RFIs have been closed.
quality: Radiographic examination of the 6-inch process pipework welds on [AREA] was completed this morning by [SUB]. Two welds returned indications within acceptance limits and one required a repair grind. The film package has been logged against the isometric drawings and passed to [COW] for review before the repair is carried out.

The hydrostatic test package for the sour water line in [AREA] was witnessed by [ER] and [COW] on Tuesday. Test pressure was held at 1.5 times design for thirty minutes with no loss recorded on the gauge. The test certificate has been signed by both parties and the line is ready for reinstatement of the flanges.

Positive material identification was carried out on twelve spool pieces delivered to laydown at [SITE]. Eleven matched the material certificates supplied by the vendor. One spool showed a chromium reading lower than expected and has been quarantined in the stores compound pending a retest by an independent laboratory.

NCR 0147 was raised after the inspector found that the galvanising thickness on the handrail brackets for the compressor deck did not meet the specification. Repainting was first proposed, but the coating supplier has advised a full strip and regalvanise. [SITE_MGR] has agreed the approach and the work will be booked with the galvaniser next week.

Torque verification on the bolted flanges for the tank farm inlet manifold was completed using a calibrated wrench. Each bolt was re-torqued in the star pattern and the values recorded on the torque sheet. Two flanges required a second pass after the gasket relaxed, and both were signed off by [SUB_CONTACT] before the joint was closed up.

The daily quality walkdown on the jetty headstock identified missing identification tags on four valve actuators. Tags were replaced from the vendor kit and the tag register updated. [CUST_PM] asked that a photograph of each tag be attached to the handover dossier so the operations team can match them to the loop drawings.

Pressure gauges used on the nitrogen purge skid were sent for recalibration to an accredited laboratory. Certificates have now been returned and checked against the instrument register. Three gauges drifted outside tolerance and have been withdrawn, with replacements fitted and recorded on the calibration log held by [PM].

Inspection and test plan hold points for the water treatment filter vessels were reviewed with [ER] at the morning meeting. Internal inspection of the underdrain laterals is now a witnessed hold point and cannot be closed without signature. Crews have been briefed that vessel closure will not be permitted until the hold has been released.

Coating dry film thickness readings were taken on the external surfaces of the 900 mm diameter pipeline sections at the stockyard. Readings were logged at every metre along each section in accordance with the specification. Two sections showed thin areas near the girth weld ends and will be overcoated after the surface is lightly abraded.

Certificates of conformity for the electrical switchgear in the substation are now complete. The package includes factory test reports, type test certificates and the manufacturer's declaration. [COW] has checked each document against the equipment schedule and confirmed that the serial numbers match the nameplates on site.

A welder qualification record for one operative on [SUB] was found to have expired the previous Friday. The welder was removed from production welding immediately and the weld log was checked back against the record. Two root runs completed during the lapse have been flagged for additional ultrasonic testing.

Test pack 14 for the gas compression module covers instrument air, nitrogen and fuel gas tie-ins. Loop checks on twenty-two transmitters are recorded as complete, with calibration certificates attached. Outstanding items include the wiring labels on the marshalling cabinet and a final continuity check on the emergency shutdown circuit.

Visual inspection of the stainless steel vessel internals was carried out before the manway covers were refitted. The inspector found a small amount of weld spatter on a support ring and recorded it on the inspection report. Cleaning and passivation of the affected area will be witnessed before the vessel is closed.

Quality records for the pipe supports on [AREA] were audited against the drawing register. Several support drawings had been superseded without the earlier revision being withdrawn from site. The document controller has issued a list of affected drawings and the site team has been asked to remove obsolete copies from the work packs.

Positive material identification results for the high alloy bolting were received from the laboratory this afternoon. All batches match the specified grade. The results have been uploaded to the document system and linked to the relevant bolt tag numbers, so the traceability chain is complete for handover.

Hydrotest pressure gauges and the chart recorder were checked against the test procedure before the isolation valves were opened. The test engineer noted that the chart paper was the wrong range, and a replacement was fetched from the stores. The test was then started again from the beginning with a fresh pressure hold.

Dimensional checks on the skid frame for the chemical dosing package were recorded against the approved fabrication drawings. Base plate levels were within tolerance, but the nozzle orientation on one vessel was rotated by about four degrees. The fabricator has been asked to submit a proposed correction for review by the design team.

Weekly quality meeting minutes were circulated to the site team and the customer representatives. Key points included a rise in minor NCRs relating to paint touch-ups, a request for better labelling of spool pieces, and confirmation that the calibration register will be audited next month by [ER].

Cable tray earthing continuity tests were completed in the process area at [SITE]. Results were logged for each tray section and any readings above the agreed limit were investigated. A loose bonding clamp was found and tightened, and the section was retested with a satisfactory result recorded on the form.

The pre-commissioning dossier index for the tank farm has been updated to show the current status of every certificate. Forty-one documents remain outstanding, mainly pump motor test reports and drawings still marked as as-built. [PM] has set a deadline for each responsible party to submit their items.

Fit-up inspection of the pipe spools for the sea water intake was completed before welding. Bevel angles, root gaps and alignment were measured and recorded. Two joints needed minor adjustment with a hydraulic clamp, and both were rechecked by the inspector before tacking was permitted.

Non-destructive testing reports for the pressure vessel nozzles were issued by the independent inspection body. Magnetic particle testing found no relevant indications on the attachment welds. The reports have been checked against the weld map and signed off by [COW], so the vessel can move to the next stage.

Material traceability for the carbon steel flanges was reviewed in the stores office. Heat numbers on several boxes were partly illegible due to weather exposure. The storekeeper transferred the information from the mill certificates, marked the boxes again and added a note to the stock record.

A toolbox talk was held on the importance of hold point signatures and the consequences of closing work before inspection. Foremen were reminded that a hold point is a stop, not a formality. Attendance was recorded and the sheet was filed with the weekly safety and quality pack.

The coating holiday test on the buried pipeline section was carried out at the trench bottom before backfill. Four small defects were found and repaired with the approved patch material. Each repair was retested at the specified voltage and the results were entered on the holiday log for [CUST_PM] to review.

Commissioning certificates for the fire water pumps were checked against the test schedule. Flow and pressure results met the specified values and the controller tests were recorded. The original factory certificate was missing one page, so the vendor has been asked to send a complete copy for the handover file.

The mechanical completion walkdown for [AREA] identified sixteen punch list items, mostly relating to missing labels, damaged insulation and a leaking drain cap. Each item was photographed and assigned to a responsible subcontractor. Close-out will be verified by the quality team before the system is handed over to operations.

The welding procedure specification for the duplex stainless steel pipework was reissued following a change of filler metal supplier. Welders were briefed on the revised interpass temperature limits and the new procedure was posted at each welding station. Old copies were collected and destroyed to avoid confusion.

Calibration of the flow meters on the custody transfer line was witnessed by [ER]. The meters were checked against a reference prover and the results were within the permitted error band. Certificates have been filed and the meter tag numbers matched to the instrument index.

Document review of the as-built drawings for the water treatment plant continued this week. Several isometrics showed valves in the wrong position, and the markups have been passed to the drawing office. A revised set will be issued once the changes have been checked against the latest site photographs and the field notes.
logistics: The reactor vessel is due on Thursday via the northern gate on a fourteen-axle trailer. The route survey and police escort were confirmed by [PM] last week. The haulier must reverse into laydown bay B3 with a banksman and a second spotter present. [SITE_MGR] will brief the lifting team before the vehicle enters the public highway.

Gate 2 will be closed to light vehicles on Saturday morning while the pipe rack steelwork is craned over the boundary fence. Site security has been asked to redirect deliveries through Gate 1 and to log all arrivals in the visitor book. Signage is being placed at the junction with Mill Lane for the duration of the lift.

The insulated pipe spools for [AREA] are arriving in six separate loads over the next three days. Each load needs a pre-booked slot at the goods reception cabin. Drivers must bring the delivery note, the material certificate copy and the photo ID that matches the booking. Late arrivals will be held at the weighbridge until a slot is free.

Laydown area C is being cleared to receive the pump skids and the associated electrical kiosks. The ground has been compacted and sleepers placed under the outriggers of the mobile crane. Please do not stack any timber or drums in this zone without checking with [PLANNER] first, as the bearing capacity has only been confirmed for the listed loads.

Our neighbour on the eastern boundary has asked for deliveries to avoid the school run between eight and nine in the morning. [CUST_PM] has agreed that all heavy vehicles will stage at the lay-by until ten past nine. Drivers will be told at the induction, and the security team will radio the gate when each vehicle is released.

The temporary power supply to the welfare compound will be switched over on Monday afternoon. The distribution board was tested by the electrician last Friday and the earth continuity readings were recorded. Anyone working on the site office kettles, heaters or chargers should unplug them before the changeover at fourteen hundred hours.

A water main shutdown has been agreed with the local supplier for Tuesday between ten and two. Hydrants on the north side will be unavailable during this window, so the fire marshals need to be told. Please fill any hand-wash stations and check the site toilet cisterns before the shutdown begins, as the supply will be off.

The customer's plant manager has requested that the flare header tie-in is planned for a night shift when the adjacent unit is in standby. [ER] will attend the pre-start meeting to confirm the isolation points. Lighting towers are to be positioned along the access road to give safe walking routes to the tie-in location.

Crane access to the tank farm is restricted by the overhead cable run near the bund wall. The lifting supervisor has marked the swing radius with yellow paint and fitted a goal post to protect the cables. All lifts over this line must be planned on the lift plan and signed off by the duty engineer before the crane is moved.

Our skip collection is scheduled for Wednesday and Friday of this week. Segregated waste containers for timber, metal, insulation and general rubbish are at the north end of the compound. Please keep lids closed and nothing loose on the ground, because the skip company will refuse any load that contains excess packaging or loose debris.

The contractor's car park has been moved to the field beyond the security fence. A minibus will run every fifteen minutes from the hardstanding at the roundabout between six and eighteen hundred. Anyone who needs to park closer for medical or mobility reasons should speak to [SITE_MGR] so a bay can be arranged at the gatehouse.

The tanker carrying nitrogen for the purge system will park on the concrete pad beside the compressor house. The driver must wear the correct PPE and remain in the vehicle cab during connection. The pad has an oil interceptor, so please keep the drain covers in place and report any spillage to the duty supervisor immediately.

Telecoms cabling for the temporary site office was damaged during trenching on Monday. The supplier has been called out and the repair is booked for tomorrow morning. Until then, the site office phone lines are down, so please use the mobile numbers on the noticeboard. Email access remains available through the portable satellite router.

Traffic management for the Ashby Road closure needs confirmation before the pipe trench is opened. The temporary traffic lights must be set to run on the approved sequence, and the signage must be checked each morning. [PM] has asked the banksman team to log any near misses and report back before the end of each shift.

The mobile crane is booked for the Thursday lift of the air cooler bundle onto the rack. Outrigger mats will be laid the day before, and the ground will be inspected by the crane supervisor. Please keep the lifting zone clear of all personnel and vehicles from six in the morning until the bundle is landed and secured.

Fire hydrant access on the east side of the unit must stay clear at all times. Two pallets of valves were found blocking the hydrant on Tuesday, and the fire officer has asked for the area to be signed. Please keep the route to the hydrant open so that a fire tender can reach it within two minutes of an alarm.

Yard staff will be moving the stored cable drums from the north field to the cable store later this week. Each drum must be checked for damage, the labels read against the schedule, and the delivery record updated. Forklift drivers should use the marked lanes and must not stack drums more than two high.

The customer has asked for the sewer connection inspection to be booked before the drainage trench is backfilled. [CUST_PM] has confirmed the inspector will attend on Friday at ten. Please leave the trench open and the pipework visible, and keep the access ladder in place so the inspector can view the joints safely.

A new laydown area has been set up behind the workshop for the bulk structural steel. The hardstanding is level, drained and fenced, but the gate lock has not yet been fitted. Until it is, please ensure the chain and padlock are secured each evening and that the key is returned to the site stores before the end of the shift.

Early morning deliveries of concrete for the pump foundations will arrive between six and seven. Batching plant drivers must use the designated wash-out area and must not discharge into the surface water drains. The banksman will guide each mixer into position, and the site engineer will sign the delivery tickets once the slump has been checked.

Our neighbour at the water treatment works has requested that all noisy hydraulic breaking work stops at four in the afternoon. [SITE_MGR] has briefed the excavation gang and posted the times on the boundary gate. Any crew that needs to work beyond four must first obtain written agreement from [ER] and inform the neighbouring operator.

The temporary generator for the commissioning phase will be delivered on the low loader on Monday. It will be placed on the bunded pad at the west corner, away from the public footpath. Refuelling must only take place with the spill tray in position, and the fuel delivery must be logged in the site register each time.

Pipe supports for the new utility corridor are being stored on timber bearers in the north field. The bearers were checked for rot and the stacks have been tied off with straps. Please do not move any support without signing it out at the stores, as the bundle numbers are needed for the erection sequence.

The overhead line crossing the site entrance has been identified as a risk to tall vehicles. Height barriers will be installed at the approach and the warning signs repositioned. Drivers of tipper trucks and mobile cranes must check the clearance before entering, and any vehicle that cannot pass safely must be turned around at the lay-by.

The site welfare cabins are being connected to the mains water supply on Wednesday. The plumber will need access to the cabin roofs and the rear service duct. Please move any personal items away from the cabin walls and ensure the taps are closed when you leave, so the pressure test can be carried out without interruption.

The customer's security team has reviewed the new access card process for the control room extension. Each contractor operative must now present a valid card at the turnstile and sign the controlled-area register. Escorted visitors will be issued with a red lanyard, and [COW] will check the register at the end of every working day.

A rolling road closure on the B-road has been arranged for the transport of the transformer on Sunday night. The route has been surveyed, the bridge loading confirmed and the lighting checked. Please make sure all site cones and barriers are returned to the depot by Monday morning so the public highway is clear for the normal traffic flow.
aob: The north access gate at [SITE] will be closed on Thursday from 14:00 to 17:00 for the drainage manhole tie-in. Insulation deliveries should use the south gate instead. [SITE_MGR] is to confirm that the traffic marshal is booked and that the revised plan is posted at the security hut before the weekend shift. Drivers arriving outside the booked windows will be held at the barrier until the marshal is available.

Crane mats for the lift on the compressor skid were found cracked at the edges during Monday's inspection. The damaged mats have been removed from the laydown area and tagged. Replacement mats are due on site next Tuesday. [PM] asked that the lift plan be reissued once the new mats are in place, with the ground bearing calculation attached for the lifting supervisor's sign-off.

A reminder that all hot work permits must be countersigned by the area authority before the grinder or welding set is brought into [AREA]. Several permits last week were found to be missing the gas test record. Permit holders should bring their own gas detector to the morning briefing, and fire watch cover must continue for thirty minutes after the final task has finished.

The jetty tide window for the cable drum offload has moved to the second week of next month because of the marine coordinator's schedule. [CUST_PM] has been informed and has agreed in principle. Lifting crews are asked to keep their availability open for that period, and the marine contractor will confirm the exact dates by Friday.

Site induction numbers have grown sharply with the arrival of the commissioning team. Some visitors have been signing in without completing the online module. Reception marshals have been asked to check each name against the induction log before issuing a pass. Anyone unable to show a valid card should be escorted to the training cabin.

Scaffold inspection tags on the tank farm bund were found to be out of date on the east elevation. The scaffolding subcontractor has been asked to re-inspect and tag the full run before the painters mobilise. Until then, the affected lifts are to be cordoned off and nobody is to work above the first lift without a written green tag.

Waste segregation at the laydown yard is still not meeting the agreed standard. Timber offcuts, metal cuttings and oily rags are being placed in the same skip. A separate skip for each waste stream has been ordered and will arrive on Monday. Until then, foremen are asked to walk their gangs through the labelled bins at the start of each shift.

The commissioning team has requested a fortnightly review of the instrument calibration certificates for the water treatment plant. Several certificates from the supplier are still awaiting signature by the independent inspector. [COW] will maintain a tracker listing each tag number, the due date and the name of the person responsible for chasing the paperwork.

Hydrotest of the 6-inch process line between the separator and the flare header is now planned for the first week of next month. The test pack needs final sign-off on the blinds register and the isolation certificates. [PLANNER] asked that the test medium supplier be given the flow rate and pressure profile by the end of this week so that the water delivery can be booked.

Heavy rain over the weekend left standing water in the pipe rack corridor and on the access road beyond the second gate. Plant operators have been asked to check the surface before driving heavy equipment across. Temporary sump pumps will be relocated to the lowest point by the drainage contractor, and the site team will report any further flooding to the weekly safety forum.

Electrical isolation certificates for the substation switchgear room need to be re-signed following the change in authorised persons on the customer side. [ER] has asked for the updated list of authorised switching personnel by Wednesday. Until the list is circulated, no one should accept a permit for switching on the 11kV panels.

The gas detection system in [AREA] has been generating nuisance alarms during the morning cleaning rounds. Engineers suspect a fault in one of the portable reference units rather than a real leak. The unit has been removed for bench checking and a spare has been issued. Operators must still respond to every alarm as normal until the cause is confirmed.

Lighting towers used on the night shift for the pipeline crossing are running low on fuel. The fuel bowser is booked for Thursday evening, but the driver has asked for the access route to be cleared of plant. [SITE_MGR] is to arrange for the fencing contractor to move the temporary barrier so that the tanker can reach the refuelling point safely.

Hard hat stickers have been issued to all supervisors this week to show their competency level. Several operatives were seen wearing old colours that no longer match the register. Supervisors should check their teams during the morning walk round and report any mismatch to the site safety adviser, who will keep the register updated.

The customer's operations team has asked for a walk through of the completed chemical dosing skid before the next steering meeting. The walk through will take about an hour and must be done with the area permit in place. [CUST_PM] has suggested a date in the week after next, subject to the commissioning schedule remaining as planned.

Vehicle movement near the crane lay down has been noted as too close to the exclusion zone on several occasions. Banksmen are reminded to hold their position at the edge of the marked boundary and not to step inside it while a lift is in progress. Dedicated signage will be placed at each corner by the end of the week.

The document control team is catching up on the vendor data books for the gas compression package. Around forty drawings marked as as-built still show earlier revisions of the piping layout. Engineering have been asked to check each sheet against the latest markup before the books are submitted to [CUSTOMER] for review.

The welfare cabin near the pipe spool fabrication shop has run out of hot water twice this week. The boiler was found to be undersized for the number of people using it during the break periods. A second heater has been ordered and should be installed by the plumbing subcontractor before the end of next week.

Permit to dig requests for the ground beside the existing flare stack are now being held until the utility survey is complete. Three requests were refused last week because the drawing did not match what was found on site. [PM] will attend the next survey briefing and confirm which excavation areas can be released for digging.

Some of the steel stored on sleepers at the east end of the yard has started to show surface rust after the wet spell. The material controller has been asked to check the certificates and mill markings before the items are moved into the covered store. Any material with heavy corrosion will be set aside for inspection.

The tank farm roof hatch covers need to be fitted with tamper seals before the customer takes over the inventory. [CUST_PM] has provided a list of seal numbers and the approved supplier. Installation crews should record each seal against the relevant hatch on the inspection sheet and return the completed sheets to the site office on Friday.

Smoking area signage at the main gate has been damaged by vehicles reversing into the post. A replacement sign has been ordered and the post will be re-set in concrete. In the meantime, a temporary sign has been put up on the fence. Supervisors are asked to remind their gangs of the designated areas during toolbox talks.

The customer's clerk of works has asked for daily photographs of the buried pipework before backfill begins along the southern route. The photographs should show the bedding, tape and marker tiles, and each should carry the chainage and date. [COW] will confirm the format at the next meeting so that the record can be filed correctly.

Nitrogen purge bottles used for the pipework closures have been left uncapped in several places. The cylinder store team has been asked to chain all bottles to the rack at the end of each shift. Any cylinder found standing unsecured will be returned to the supplier and replaced on the next delivery.

The noise survey for the water treatment plant will be repeated next week because some readings were taken during a period of heavy plant use. Crews are asked to keep the rotary drills and the diesel compressor off the plant between 10:00 and 11:30 on the survey days. The acoustic consultant will issue the timetable on Monday.

Sub-contractor labour sign-in sheets are not being completed at the gate on the early shift. The gatehouse has been given a revised sheet that lists company name, trade, and reporting location. [SUB] managers are to ensure their supervisors complete the sheet before leaving the gatehouse, and the site office will spot check the records each week.

The fire water header test on the jetty approach is scheduled for the second Monday of next month. The fire marshals need to be told in advance so that the sprinkler cover can be arranged for the temporary office block. [SITE_MGR] to confirm with the fire service that the hydrant will be available and that the test will be witnessed.

Cable tray supports on the north side of [AREA] are missing their earthing straps in several locations. The electrical foreman has listed the affected positions on a marked-up layout and will rectify them on the afternoon shift. A second check will be made by the independent electrical inspector before the containment is closed up.

Lunchtime access to the pipe rack walkway has been restricted because of the scaffold modification underway. Operatives are reminded that the walkway is closed and that the alternative route via the service stair must be used. Any person found on the walkway during the closure will be removed from the site for the rest of the day.

The team handover register for the gas compression area has several gaps where signatures have been left blank. Each discipline lead is asked to review the entries for their own systems and sign off the pages before the register is closed for the week. Blank pages will be struck through and initialled by the document controller.
cvr_general: The cash position for [PROJECT] was reviewed at the internal contract cost review on Tuesday. Receipts against the monthly payment application are expected to clear within the agreed terms, and finance confirmed that payroll and subcontract payments are covered for the next five weeks. [PM] asked finance to flag any slippage in customer remittances by Thursday so the site team can plan purchasing accordingly.

The monthly application for payment for [AREA] was submitted to [CUSTOMER] on the due date. [QS] checked the measured quantities against the site records and the supporting certificates before release. [ER] has acknowledged receipt and indicated that the assessment will be reviewed at the next progress meeting.

Site headcount for the week stood at 142 across mechanical, piping and electrical trades. Two electricians transferred from [SUB] to cover the cable tray installation in [AREA], and the timesheet reconciliation for the period is now complete. [SITE_MGR] will confirm the shift pattern for the commissioning crew by Friday.

Long-lead items for the tank farm remain on track. The pressure transmitters have been received at the laydown yard and inspected against the datasheets, with two units returned for a minor nameplate correction. Expediting reports will be circulated weekly until the remaining valves are delivered.

Subcontract payment runs were discussed in detail. [SUB_CONTACT] queried the timing of the next remittance and was advised that funds from [CUSTOMER] are scheduled for the usual cycle. Finance will issue a short note to all package managers confirming the payment calendar for the remainder of the quarter.

Subcontract applications for civils works in [AREA] were logged and checked for compliance with the rate schedule. Two were returned for missing timesheets and one was held pending signed inspection test plans. Resubmission is expected before the cut-off date set by the commercial team.

Recruitment for the commissioning engineer role is progressing. Three candidates have completed interviews and references are being taken up. Until the post is filled, [PM] has agreed that the existing lead engineer will supervise the loop checks on the gas compression skid, with weekly updates to [CUST_PM].

Structural steel for the jetty head was delivered in two batches this week. Mill certificates were matched to the heat numbers on each member, and the surface treatment records were filed with the material traceability log. Remaining sections are scheduled to arrive once the fabrication shop completes the bracing.

Retention balances were noted in the cash review. The team agreed that release timing will follow completion of the punch lists for each area. Finance has asked site to keep handover documents current so that the release can proceed without administrative hold-ups.

The application for payment covering the water treatment package was prepared using the agreed progress methodology. [QS] reconciled the percentage complete with the planner's updated schedule and the earned value report. A copy was sent to [COW] for information before submission to [ER].

Labour absence figures for the month were reviewed. Sickness levels were slightly below the norm, and one welder has been moved to day shift after a medical review. Induction records for the three new starters on the substation package are complete and held in the site office.

Purchase orders for consumables were checked against the bill of materials. Gaskets, bolting and insulation kits are now fully covered for the next phase, and the remaining requisitions are pending approval from the package manager. Supplier acknowledgements have been chased for two suppliers who are running behind.

Cash flow for the coming month was discussed briefly. Income from the customer is expected at the usual point, and outgoings for plant hire and fuel are in line with the planned payment schedule held by finance. No additional borrowing requirement was identified at this stage.

Supplier invoices for the tank farm pipework were matched to goods received notes and purchase orders. Three invoices were queried over unit descriptions and have been returned to the supplier for correction. Matching will be completed before the close of the accounting period.

Application for the commissioning phase was drafted and circulated internally for comment. Supporting evidence includes completed test records, the updated punch list and photographs of the finished works. [PM] will sign the covering letter once the attachments are checked.

Crane operator certification was checked for all lifting personnel working on the jetty. Two operators hold current ticket renewals, and one certificate is due for renewal next month. [SITE_MGR] has booked the training provider and will confirm dates to the lifting supervisor.

The electrical switchgear for the substation is due on site in six weeks. Factory acceptance testing has been scheduled and [CUSTOMER] has been invited to witness the tests. Delivery paperwork, including the packing list and certificates of conformity, will be checked before the unit is offloaded.

Payment to the plant hire company was made on time, and the remittance advice was filed against the cost code reference. The team noted that the next hire invoice will include an additional compressor, and finance will plan for this within the existing payment run.

Welfare facilities at the north compound were inspected by the safety team. Drying room capacity was reduced during the week and the contractor has agreed to provide an additional unit. Toolbox talks have been updated to remind crews of the revised access route to [AREA].

Scaffold materials were reconciled against the erection schedule. Surplus tube and fittings have been returned to the yard and recorded on the stock sheet. Remaining orders will be placed once the access plan for the pipe rack has been confirmed by the planning team.

The accruals listing for the month was reviewed with finance. Several goods received items were not yet invoiced, and site staff agreed to confirm receipt dates so the accruals can be accurate. Any missing confirmations will be followed up before the period closes.

The customer's review of the last application requested additional supporting documentation for the pipeline welding records. [QS] has pulled the weld maps and inspection reports and will issue a clarification note to [ER] by the end of the week.

Overtime hours for the shutdown crew were approved in line with the agreed rota. Planning has allocated night shift cover for the hot work permits, and supervisors have confirmed that rest breaks will be maintained for all personnel working extended hours.

Instrument cable drums are being tracked against the cable schedule. Two drums have been cut short and the remaining lengths are being recorded on the cable register. Replacement stock has been requested from the supplier, with delivery expected before loop testing starts.

Customer remittance dates were confirmed with the office of [CUST_PM]. The team agreed that any delay will be raised at the progress meeting rather than through informal channels. Finance will keep a running log of expected receipts so that cash planning remains realistic.

The monthly summary of applications for the gas compression package was circulated. Submitted, approved and pending items are shown in separate columns, with comments from [COW] added where inspection evidence is still awaited. The summary will be reviewed again at the next cost review meeting.

The supervisory structure for the water treatment area was confirmed. [SUB] will provide a foreman for the pipework crew, and an experienced fitter has been appointed as deputy. Handover arrangements between the day and night teams have been written into the site instructions.

Coatings for the tank shell were delivered to the approved storage container. Batch numbers were recorded against the material certificates and shelf life was checked. The applicator has confirmed that environmental conditions will be monitored before blasting begins.

The team reviewed the position on petty cash and site imprest accounts. Balances are within the agreed limits, and receipts for the last fortnight have been submitted for reconciliation. Finance has asked that all purchases under the approved threshold be recorded on the standard form.

Internal approval of the monthly submission for [PROJECT] was given at the review. Actions include updating the planner's schedule, confirming measured quantities for the pipe supports and sending revised progress photographs to [CUST_PM] for the record. [PM] will chair the follow-up call.
diary: 07:15 Toolbox talk held at the main gate for 22 operatives on working at height around the [AREA] pipe rack. Attendance sheet signed and filed. Scaffold inspection tag checked on level 2 before access was granted to the fitters. No issues raised by the crew, though the banksman rota needs confirming for Thursday night shift.

Visit from [COW] at 10:30 to walk the [AREA] compressor skid. He queried the torque records for the flange bolting on the suction line and asked for copies of the calibration certificates for the wrench. Records were pulled from the document room and handed over before he left the area around noon.

Hydrotest of the 6-inch firewater header completed on the north run. Pressure held at 12 barg for the full ten-minute hold with no visible weeping at the flanges. Test pump was isolated and drained, and the gauge calibration sticker was checked against the test pack. Results sent to [PM] for sign-off this afternoon.

Overcast and light rain from 13:00, so the crane lift for the air cooler bundle was postponed until conditions improve. Lifting supervisor and [SUB_CONTACT] agreed to reconvene at 07:00 tomorrow. Slinging equipment has been returned to the store and the exclusion zone barrier left in place around the lift footprint.

Water treatment package at [SITE] had its second fill of dosing chemical delivered by tanker. Bunded area inspected afterwards with no spillage found. Delivery docket checked against the chemical safety data sheet and the bund drain valve confirmed closed. Operator on shift has been reminded of the transfer procedure.

Gas detection function test carried out on the [AREA] skid with the instrument technician. Two sensors on the east side gave slow responses and were recalibrated using span gas. Both were retested and logged as passing. The panel reset was checked by the commissioning engineer before close of shift.

Morning walk around the tank farm with [SITE_MGR] to check bunding integrity after last night's rainfall. Standing water pumped out through the oil-interceptor route and a sample taken for visual check. Hose connection at tank T-104 was found loose and tightened. Housekeeping on the containment slab noted for the afternoon crew.

Jetty deck inspection by the [ER] team at 09:00. Fender pads checked for damage and mooring bollard load markings confirmed as legible. Two handrail brackets flagged for re-fixing. Lifting beam certificate requested for the file. Marine coordinator will confirm the berth window with the port authority by Friday.

Pipeline welders on the river crossing reported a shortage of consumables for the root pass. Stores have been asked to rush the replacement rods from the main depot. Weld procedure qualification records were checked and found current. Inspector booked for radiography on the first three joints on Monday.

Substation energisation paperwork reviewed with [CUST_PM]. Switching schedule agreed for the 33 kV feeder outage next Saturday. Earthing certificates need countersigning by the authorised person before permit issue. Mobile generator for the temporary supply has been confirmed for delivery at 06:00 on the day.

Visitors from the insurance surveyor's office toured the process area with [PM] and [SITE_MGR]. Questions focused on fire water coverage at the flare knock-out drum and the location of the nearest eyewash station. Sketches were marked up on site and the surveyor requested a copy of the latest hazard register.

Pump P-203A tripped on high vibration during the run-in test. Coupling alignment was checked with dial gauges and found within tolerance, so suspicion moved to the bearing housing. Vendor rep called in remotely. Pump isolated and locked off until the bearing inspection is complete tomorrow morning.

Civil gang poured the bund wall section for the chemical store. Concrete delivered in two loads from the batching plant and cube samples taken at the truck. Vibration applied to the formwork to avoid honeycombing. Curing compound applied to the exposed faces before the crew left at 17:00.

Scaffold handover for the reactor platform completed by [SUB] with the inspection tag signed off. Handrails and toe boards checked against the scaffold design drawing. Two loose ledgers at the east end were tightened on the spot. Permit holders were briefed before access was granted.

Lockout tagout audit on the compressor house. Three isolation points were found without the correct padlock colour coding, and the isolation certificate for the gas line was missing a signature. Supervisor corrected both during the walk. Refresher reminder sent to all authorised persons in the area.

Crane inspection carried out on the 60-tonne mobile unit by the third-party inspector. Load chart and outrigger pads checked, along with the wire rope on the main hoist. Certificate of thorough examination issued and displayed in the cab. Operator confirmed the anti-two-block device was working correctly.

Pipe rack painting progressed along grid lines C to F on the second tier. Surface preparation checked with a surface profile gauge and found acceptable. Paint batch numbers recorded on the inspection log. Ambient temperature and dew point readings taken at 10:00 and 14:00 as required.

Electrical isolation for the MCC room completed by the site electricians. Permit to work cancelled once the test equipment had been removed from the cubicle. Fire extinguisher inspection tags checked during the walk round. A tool left in the cable tray was retrieved and returned to the toolbox.

Site induction given to six new starters from [SUB] before they were allowed onto the plot. Emergency assembly points shown on the site map and the siren test witnessed at 08:30. Induction cards issued and entered on the attendance register. Medical declaration forms collected and filed.

Reviewed the sump pump alarm on the water treatment skid after it sounded during the night. Float switch found stuck in the up position due to debris. Cleaned and tested by the instrument fitter, and now working correctly. Night shift operator informed and the alarm log updated accordingly.

Weather hold called at 14:30 when wind gusts reached the limit for the telehandler on the laydown area. Materials secured and the boom lowered to stowed position. Crew moved to the workshop for a housekeeping session. Work resumes when the anemometer reading falls below the limit on the wind sheet.

Visit by the customer's operations team to review the commissioning sequence for the gas export line. Walked the route from the metering skid to the pig receiver. They asked for updated purge records and wanted the nitrogen supply isolation shown on the drawing. Follow-up meeting booked for Wednesday.

Concrete foundations for the new transformer bay checked against the setting-out drawing. Anchor bolt positions within tolerance on the survey report. Rebar cover measured at four points before the pour was approved. Survey team to re-check levels at the north corner tomorrow.

Tank T-202 gauging system calibrated by the instrument team. Level transmitter zeroed and spanned against the calibrated reference. Results witnessed by the customer's inspector and signed on the test sheet. Radar gauge alarm setpoints confirmed against the cause and effect matrix.

Cable tray installation on the rack west of the control room progressed by 40 metres. Cable routing checked against the tray layout drawing and segregation between power and instrument cables confirmed. Earth bonding straps fitted at each joint. Checklist signed by the electrical foreman.

Hot work permit issued for the cutting of the old flare line spool. Fire watch assigned for the full task plus thirty minutes after completion. Gas test readings taken at the start, midpoint and finish, all showing zero LEL. Permit closed out and returned to the permit office at 16:15.

Delivery of insulation materials arrived at the gate, two pallets short against the advice note. Stores clerk logged the discrepancy and the supplier was contacted before the driver left. Remaining pallets off-loaded to the laydown bay and checked against the packing list. Damaged cartons photographed for the record.

Morning meeting with [PLANNER] to review the look-ahead for the next two weeks. Priority given to the hydrotest packages on the north side. Crane availability confirmed for the heat exchanger lift on the 14th. Concern raised about the late arrival of the instrument cable drums.

Pressure relief valve for the nitrogen package sent away for testing and a replacement unit collected from the vendor's depot. Tag number checked against the valve schedule and the certificate filed with the handover pack. Installation to be witnessed by the inspector on Monday morning.

Late shift handover completed at 19:00. Outstanding items: scaffold tag on the reactor platform to be re-inspected, gas detector recalibration in progress, and the jetty mooring line inspection still open. Night supervisor briefed and radio channel confirmed. Site secured and gate log signed.
